policy_title: Expand pay-gap protections and support flexible working
stated: Push for pay-gap protections to be extended to all protected characteristics, including ethnicity, disability, and sexual orientation, ensuring equal pay for equal work and flexible working arrangements.

source.quote: Green MPs will push for pay-gap protections to be extended to all protected characteristics including ethnicity, disability and sexual orientation. We believe in equal pay for equal work and in the right to flexible working arrangements that will benefit women, carers and disabled people in particular.

bearing_set.reason: Extending pay-gap protections to additional characteristics and mandating flexible working directly bears on pay equity, employment rights, and job quality for affected workers.
Expanding anti-discrimination protections to cover ethnicity, disability, and sexual orientation pay gaps is a substantive equal-treatment measure, squarely within O9's anti-discrimination scope.
Closing pay gaps across ethnicity, disability, and sexual orientation would directly narrow income inequality between protected groups and the majority, moving the inter-group earnings gap indicator.

membership_note: Three fundamentals: the policy simultaneously acts on labour-market fairness (O4), anti-discrimination law (O9), and the income gap between groups (O14). A fiscal/O12 bearing was considered but no material public-spending or borrowing mechanism is specified. An O10 (employer mandates) bearing was considered but the coercive burden falls on businesses rather than individuals, and the mechanism does not clearly move a core O10 indicator (speech, bodily autonomy, surveillance).
